newsitem.title: USA: Psychemedics sells drug test service to consumers.
newsitem.headline: Psychemedics sells drug test service to consumers.

text.p: Psychemedics Corp will begin selling its hair analysis drug testing services to consumers this weekend at Walgreen Co stores, the company's president said on Wednesday.

The Cambridge, Massachusetts headquartered firm, which usually serves corporations and municipalities who test their workers for drug use, will be making its services available to consumers, Psychemedics President Raymond Kubacki, Jr. said in a telephone interview.

At $59.95 a test, a consumer can collect a hair sample and send it to the company's laboratory, based in Culver City, Calif., where it will be tested for marijuana, cocaine, opiates, methamphetamines and PCP. The tests can determine whether any of these substances have been used within the last 90 days, Kubacki said.
"We're not changing our focus," Kubacki said. "We're making this available because we had a lot of requests from parents for our patented technology."
The test, known as PDT-90, is the company's only product.
